tasks.notes: lib/db/prisma.ts exports a singleton PrismaClient wired to Prisma 7's mandatory driver adapter (`@prisma/adapter-pg`). Key choices: (1) adapter-pg over adapter-neon — Render runs a long-lived Node process against the Neon pooler URL, the HTTP serverless adapter is for edge/serverless cold-start runtimes we don't target. (2) `pg` is a transitive dep of `@prisma/adapter-pg@7.8.0` — no need to install it separately (verified in adapter's package.json). (3) `import 'server-only'` at the top so an accidental client-component import fails at build time. (4) Singleton uses `globalThis.__beatyourselfPrisma` cache, gated on `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` — in prod a fresh client per worker, in dev HMR reuses the cached instance to keep Neon's free-tier connection cap from being exhausted. (5) Variable name `__beatyourselfPrisma` (not generic `__prisma`) to avoid colliding with any other Prisma installs in node_modules. Verification (all pass): `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run build` (production build emits the prisma module without errors); functional smoke against Neon via a one-off node script (`new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg(DATABASE_URL) }).user.findMany()` → []; `.challenge.findMany()` → []); HMR singleton smoke: started `npm run dev` with env vars piped from .env.local, hit a temporary `/api/smoke-prisma` route 5 times across 3 HMR file-touches on lib/db/prisma.ts and the route itself — every response was `{userCount:0,challengeCount:0}` and the dev-server log shows zero Prisma instance warnings. tasks.notes: lib/crypto/cipher.ts exports encrypt/decrypt using node:crypto AES-256-GCM with a 12-byte IV (NIST SP 800-38D recommended length) and 16-byte auth tag. Wire format is `iv:authTag:ciphertext` with each segment base64. Key handling: cipher reads process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY at call time (not module-load time) so unit tests can stub the key without satisfying the full @/config/env zod schema; this also means the env validator's broader checks still apply when the Next.js runtime boots. Key accepts either 64-char hex or 44-char base64 (validated to land at 32 bytes after decode). `import 'server-only'` at top of cipher.ts blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. Test infra: installed vitest@4.1.5 + @vitest/coverage-v8; vitest.config.ts aliases `server-only` to test/server-only-shim.ts (no-op) and `@/*` to project root. npm scripts added: `test` (vitest run) and `test:watch` (vitest). 10 unit tests (lib/crypto/cipher.test.ts) cover: round-trip with edge cases (empty, unicode, 10k-char, JSON tokens); unique IV per encrypt; wire format (iv=12 bytes, authTag=16 bytes, ct>0); ciphertext tampering throws; auth-tag tampering throws; malformed payload throws; wrong-key decrypt throws; base64 key works alongside hex; missing key throws; wrong-length key throws. tasks.notes: Installed next-auth@5.0.0-beta.31 (Auth.js v5; supports Next 16 per peerDeps). Strategy=jwt, maxAge=60*60*24*30 (30 days). trustHost=true (single-host Render deploy; required for Auth.js to accept the proxied X-Forwarded-Host). Single Google provider with authorization params {prompt:'consent', access_type:'offline', response_type:'code'} so we always get a refresh_token (per the @auth/core/providers/google docs note: Google only returns refresh_token on first consent unless prompt=consent is forced). pages.signIn='/login' so unauthenticated redirects from auth() / requireSession() land at the page TASK-008 will create. Whitelist + user provisioning is in the signIn callback (fail closed): (1) reject if account.provider !== 'google'; (2) reject if !profile.email_verified (defends against unverified Google accounts); (3) reject if no email or no profile.sub; (4) if env.ALLOWED_EMAIL is set, require case-insensitive match — when ALLOWED_EMAIL is unset (zod-optional), allow any verified Google email so tasks.json's PRD test_step 'Войти с НЕ-whitelist-email — отказ' is testable only when ALLOWED_EMAIL is configured. (5) prisma.user.upsert keyed on the compound unique (provider, providerId) — Prisma 7 generates the relation key as `provider_providerId` (verified at runtime via smoke). tasks.notes: lib/services/challenges.ts exports createChallenge / getChallenge / listChallenges / updateChallenge / deleteChallenge. Pure service layer per architectural_principles ('тонкий service layer: services вызывают Prisma напрямую, без репозиториев'). All five functions take userId as first arg and scope every where-clause by userId for IDOR protection. Design choices: (1) createChallenge does NOT explicitly set status — relies on the schema default ChallengeStatus.active and createdAt default now() (verified in schema.prisma:111,113). currentValue defaults to 0 (line 112). Avoids two sources of truth for the same default. (2) listChallenges accepts {status?, year?}. Year filter uses calendar-overlap interpretation: a challenge belongs to year Y if [startDate, endDate] intersects [Jan 1 Y, Dec 31 Y] — implemented as startDate ≤ Dec31(Y) AND endDate ≥ Jan1(Y). This matches TASK-031's archive-by-year filter (challenges that ran during a year, not just ended in it). orderBy is [status asc, createdAt desc] so 'active' challenges naturally surface above 'archived'/'completed'/'failed' in the same list. (3) updateChallenge first findFirst({id, userId}) → returns null on miss (covers IDOR + nonexistent). For owners: re-fetches existing row and validates input.endDate.getTime() >= existing.startDate.getTime() before writing. Throws Error('End date must be on or after the challenge start date') on violation — TASK-010 progress flagged that this validation has to live in the service since updateChallengeSchema can't see startDate. (4) Update payload built field-by-field with `if (input.X !== undefined)` so `null`-explicit clearing of optional fields (description/color/icon) still works correctly while undefined fields are skipped. Uses Prisma.ChallengeUpdateInput type. (5) deleteChallenge uses findFirst({id, userId}) → null-on-miss → delete({id}). Two-query pattern is fine for user-scoped ops; deleteMany({id, userId}) would only return a count, but TASK-011 spec implies returning the deleted row (typed return per acceptance criteria). Race window between findFirst and delete is irrelevant for single-user ops. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client-bundle leak (cascade from prisma singleton, but explicit at the service boundary too). tasks.notes: actions/challenges.ts begins with 'use server' so all exports are Server Actions per the React Server Functions contract (verified against node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/07-mutating-data.md — Next 16 keeps the directive + revalidatePath('next/cache') API from earlier versions). Exports: createChallengeAction(input), updateChallengeAction(id, input), deleteChallengeAction(id) plus an ActionResult<T> = {success:true,data:T}|{success:false,error:string} discriminated union. Each action calls requireSession() FIRST (per acceptance criterion 3 + test_step 2 'Без сессии — action бросает unauthorized') — requireSession() in lib/auth/session.ts calls auth() then redirect('/login') from next/navigation when session.user.id is missing, which throws NEXT_REDIRECT (a control-flow exception that Next handles by returning a 307). This IS the 'throws unauthorized' behavior required by test_step 2: the action does not return a success result for un-authed callers. Returning an explicit {success:false,error:'Unauthorized'} would be wrong here because the redirect is the user-facing UX (they land on /login) — same pattern as protected (app)/* pages from TASK-008. Then each mutating action runs zod safeParse via createChallengeSchema / updateChallengeSchema (delegates the schema rules from TASK-010 — title min/max, targetValue>0, endDate>=startDate, color regex, plus updateSchema strips read-only fields metric/targetValue/type/startDate/title — exercised in the smoke). On parse failure: returns {success:false, error: '<path>: <message>; ...'} via formatZodError helper that joins all issues with '; ' so a form can show them all at once. Then calls the service from lib/services/challenges.ts (TASK-011) — the service's IDOR scoping (userId in every where-clause) means cross-user ids return null and surface as {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}. The service's endDate<startDate guard for updateChallenge throws an Error which the action catches and surfaces as {success:false, error:<message>}. STRUCTURAL CHOICE worth flagging: revalidatePath calls happen AFTER the try/catch around the mutation, NOT inside it. Reason: if revalidatePath throws (e.g., misconfigured cacheComponents in the future, or a Next internals bug), that should NOT be reported to the caller as a mutation failure — the DB write already succeeded. The current shape: mutate inside try/catch → on failure return {success:false}; on success exit the try block, run revalidateChallengeViews(), then return {success:true,data}. revalidateChallengeViews() always revalidates /challenges + /dashboard (per acceptance criterion 5 'revalidatePath("/challenges") и/или revalidatePath("/dashboard")'), and additionally /challenges/[id] for create+update so the detail page (TASK-032) sees fresh data. delete revalidates only the list views, not /challenges/[id] (the page is going to 404 anyway). VERIFICATION (per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file): wrote temporary actions/_smoke-challenges.test.ts (10 vitest cases against live Neon, deleted after run) covering all three PRD test_steps + IDOR + edge cases. Mocked @/lib/auth/session.requireSession via vi.hoisted+vi.mock so the test can flip session identity per case (owner vs. cross-user) and simulate the no-session redirect throw. Also mocked next/cache.revalidatePath because vitest has no Next.js request context — calling it bare yields 'Invariant: static generation store missing in revalidatePath /challenges'. This is a TEST-CONTEXT issue only, not a production issue (real server-action POSTs always have the request context); the mock just lets the action run end-to-end without a Next renderer. Cases (10/10 passed): (1) createChallengeAction valid input → {success:true} with userId=ownerId, status='active', currentValue=0, row in DB; (2) createChallengeAction invalid input (empty title + targetValue=0 + endDate<startDate) → {success:false, error contains 'title','targetValue','endDate'}; (3) updateChallengeAction owner editable fields (description+endDate) → row updated in DB; (4) updateChallengeAction stripped fields (targetValue=999, metric='steps') do NOT mutate the DB row — schema strips them, only description applied; (5) updateChallengeAction cross-user id → {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}, target row unchanged in DB; (6) updateChallengeAction with endDate<startDate via service throw → {success:false, error matches /end date/i}; (7) deleteChallengeAction owner → {success:true, data.id matches}, findUnique returns null afterwards; (8) deleteChallengeAction cross-user → {success:false, error:'Challenge not found'}, target row remains in DB; (9) deleteChallengeAction with empty id → {success:false, error:'Challenge id is required'} (the inline guard, no DB touch); (10) createChallengeAction without session → requireSessionMock throws synthetic NEXT_REDIRECT error → action propagates, awaited promise rejects with /NEXT_REDIRECT/. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run build (✓ Compiled successfully in 2.0s; routes registered: same 7 as TASK-008 — actions are not separate routes, they're served via the existing route handlers' POST). NOTE for TASK-013/014/015 (next pending challenges UI tasks): action signature is createChallengeAction(input: unknown) — input arrives as a plain object from react-hook-form's submit handler. With z.coerce.date() in createChallengeSchema, ISO date strings 'YYYY-MM-DD' work as-is from <input type=date>. ActionResult<T> is exported, so form code can do `if (result.success) toast.success('создано') else toast.error(result.error)`. NOTE: requireSession throws NEXT_REDIRECT in the un-authed path — the form's onSubmit must NOT swallow it; let it propagate so Next.js sends the 307 to /login. NOTE for TASK-038 (empty states / error UX): the {success:false,error:string} shape is consumer-friendly for shadcn sonner toast.error(error). Multi-issue zod errors come back as a single string joined with '; ' — fine for an inline form-level toast; if you want field-level errors, switch to returning the issue list and have the form set errors via setError per path. Doesn't block TASK-013/014/015 at the contract level.

tasks.notes: lib/validation/activity.ts exports createActivitySchema, updateActivitySchema, plus inferred types CreateActivityInput / UpdateActivityInput. Built on zod 4.3.6 with z.enum(ActivityType) using Prisma 7's runtime enum object directly — same pattern as TASK-010 (challenge.ts) for single-source-of-truth with the DB. Field rules: activityType required on create / optional on update; distanceKm and durationMin are z.number().nonnegative().optional() (Float? in schema.prisma); steps is z.number().int().nonnegative().optional() (Int? in schema.prisma — integer enforced at the schema layer); note z.string().trim().max(500).optional() (matches VarChar(500) in schema.prisma:134); activityDate z.coerce.date() — required+defaulted-to-new-Date() on create, optional on update. Cross-field refine on create: at least one of distanceKm/durationMin/steps must be > 0 (data.X ?? 0 > 0 across all three). Refine path is ['distanceKm'] so the error surfaces on the metric group in form UIs. updateActivitySchema is a fresh z.object (NOT .partial() of create) with NO refine — service layer (TASK-017) is responsible for any merged-state invariant checks. Empty {} update is valid (e.g., for revalidating only). Per architectural_principles 'Тесты пишем ТОЛЬКО для streak calculation и token crypto' — no permanent unit tests added; verified via one-off node --experimental-strip-types script (33/33 cases) covering: PRD test_steps (parse({}) rejected, valid run+5km, note>500 rejected); 'at least one metric > 0' refine (activityType-only rejected, all-zero metrics rejected, duration-only valid, steps-only valid); activityDate default-to-now and ISO coercion; all three ActivityType enum values + invalid value rejection; negative metric rejection; integer-only steps; note trim+max=500 boundary; distanceKm string rejection (no implicit coercion); fractional distance/duration accepted; updateActivitySchema accepts empty/partial/multiple-field updates, rejects negative metrics + oversize note + non-integer steps, strips unknown keys (defense against DevTools spoof of source/externalId — those are server-controlled in TASK-017 service layer). Verification (all clean): npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 — 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress unaffected), npm run build (with shell-overridden env since .env.local has the known TASK-003 NEXTAUTH_URL typo). Note for TASK-017: activityDate default = new Date() (current instant). Per TASK-021's UTC-midnight calendar-day convention, the service layer must normalize activityDate to UTC-midnight matching the user's tz calendar day before write — the schema layer can't do this without tz context. Also note: 'source' and 'externalId' are NOT in the schema (manual creates always set source='manual' in service; Strava ingestion takes a separate code path).

All mutating functions call recalculateChallengeProgress(userId) from @/lib/services/challenge-progress-recalc after the DB write succeeds. Same pattern as challenges.ts: free functions, userId is always the first arg and scopes every where-clause for IDOR protection. Design choices: (1) createActivity takes a third `source` param defaulting to 'manual' per TASK-017 spec; the action layer for the Strava sync path uses createStravaActivity instead. (2) createStravaActivity uses Prisma's compound-unique upsert via `where: { externalId_source: { externalId, source: 'strava' } }` (the auto-generated key name from `@@unique([externalId, source])` in schema.prisma:140). The same `data` object is reused for create + update — second call with the same externalId edits the existing row, no duplicate insert. Activity.externalId is nullable schema-wide so manual rows can legally store NULL; createStravaActivity requires non-null externalId at the type boundary. (4) listActivities filter supports {from, to, source}. (5) Activity.activityDate is @db.Date so timestamp comparisons map to calendar-day comparisons (UTC midnight per Prisma 7). Per TASK-021 progress notes, calendar-day-vs-user-tz-day normalization is the responsibility of the caller (form/Strava-sync layer) — service just passes Date through. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. tasks.notes: Split into two files to keep the pure function unit-testable without DB env. lib/services/challenge-progress.ts exports calculateProgress(challenge, activities) plus ProgressActivity / ProgressChallenge types — NO server-only or prisma imports. lib/services/challenge-progress-recalc.ts exports recalculateChallengeProgress(userId, options?) which does the I/O. Reason for split: the pure module is imported into vitest tests directly; if it transitively pulled in @/lib/db/prisma → @/config/env, vitest would fail at module load on missing DATABASE_URL/NEXTAUTH_*/GOOGLE_* (verified — first run failed exactly this way). Pure module mirrors lib/services/streaks.ts pattern (also no prisma import, also unit-tested per architectural_principles 'Тесты пишем ТОЛЬКО для streak calculation и token crypto' — TASK-019 acceptance explicitly requires unit tests, so progress joins streak + crypto in the test bucket). Design: (1) calculateProgress filters activities by [startDate, endDate] inclusive on both ends — startDate/endDate are @db.Date (UTC midnight per Prisma 7 deserialization, same convention as Activity.activityDate per TASK-021 notes), so timestamp-equality comparison is calendar-day-equality. (2) For type='cumulative' returns SUM by metric across in-period activities. For type='single_day' buckets by UTC day key (toISOString().slice(0,10)) and returns MAX per-day sum. (3) Metric mapping: steps→Activity.steps, distance_km→distanceKm, duration_min→durationMin (all nullable, treated as 0), runs_count→COUNT WHERE activityType='run', custom→0 (placeholder; if a future user-defined metric needs evaluation, calculateProgress's caller must compute it). switch has exhaustiveness guard via `const _exhaustive: never = metric`. (4) recalculateChallengeProgress fetches active challenges (optionally one by id), finds the widest [earliestStart..latestEnd] window across them, makes ONE prisma.activity.findMany call for that window with `select` to avoid pulling note/createdAt/stravaData, then issues per-challenge prisma.challenge.update inside a single $transaction. (5) Sticky completion: if currentValue >= targetValue, sets status='completed' and completedAt=now. Re-running recalc on a completed challenge is a no-op since the active-status filter excludes it — matches PRD intent (deletes/decreases don't un-complete a finished challenge). (6) Failed-by-deadline transition is OUT of scope here — that belongs to TASK-020's cron endpoint (status='active' AND endDate < today AND currentValue < target → 'failed'). 18 unit tests in lib/services/challenge-progress.test.ts cover: PRD example cumulative (30+40+35=105), PRD example single_day steps (30k+25k same day, 10k other → 55k), all four numeric metrics for cumulative, runs_count counts only ActivityType.run, custom returns 0, empty array → 0, null fields treated as 0 across mismatched metrics, single_day picks max not last, single_day distance_km sum-per-day, single_day runs_count counts max-runs-in-a-day, period boundaries (activity exactly on startDate/endDate counted; one day before/after excluded), mixed in/out filter, input array purity. Verification (all clean): npm test 44/44 (10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm run build (with shell-overridden env since .env.local has the known TASK-003 NEXTAUTH_URL typo). recalculateChallengeProgress was NOT smoke-tested against Neon — it's straightforward Prisma I/O around a tested pure function, and TASK-017 (Activity service) will exercise it end-to-end as the first caller; deferred verification there is more honest than a synthetic smoke.

tasks.notes: app/api/cron/check-deadlines/route.ts exports POST(request: Request). Single-query implementation via prisma.$executeRaw with Prisma.sql template: UPDATE challenges SET status='failed' WHERE status='active' AND end_date < CURRENT_DATE AND current_value < target_value. Returns { processed: N } where N is the row count returned by $executeRaw. Auth gate: reads env.CRON_SECRET (optional in zod schema → returns 503 if not configured); compares the full 'Bearer <secret>' header with timingSafeEqual (length-checks first to avoid timingSafeEqual throwing on mismatched lengths). Design choices worth flagging: (1) Used $executeRaw with Prisma.sql, NOT $executeRawUnsafe — Prisma.sql is parameterized, but here there are no user inputs anyway; the $executeRaw + Prisma.sql combo is the canonical Prisma 7 idiom for fixed SQL with safe interpolation. (2) Used CURRENT_DATE (Postgres) instead of computing 'today' in JS and passing it as a parameter. Reason: end_date is @db.Date (UTC midnight per Prisma 7 deserialization, same convention as Activity.activityDate per TASK-021's notes). 'end_date < CURRENT_DATE' is a calendar-day comparison in the DB's timezone (UTC for Neon). Since the schema-wide convention is UTC-midnight = calendar day, comparing against CURRENT_DATE (which Postgres evaluates as the current UTC calendar day on a UTC-configured server like Neon) is correct. A multi-tz-per-user system would need per-user evaluation, but the PRD has a single user and the current convention is uniform UTC; future per-user-tz work belongs to a separate task. (3) Used Prisma's typed updateMany alternatives considered: Prisma supports field-vs-field comparisons via prisma.challenge.fields.targetValue references but not in updateMany's where clause for Float column comparisons reliably across versions — the raw SQL is simpler, single-query, and atomic. (4) Idempotent by construction: after the first call flips matching rows to status='failed', the WHERE clause no longer matches them (status='active' filter), so subsequent calls return 0. (5) Auth comparison uses node:crypto timingSafeEqual on Buffer.from(header) vs Buffer.from('Bearer ' + secret); explicit length check first because timingSafeEqual throws on length mismatch in Node >=16. The TASK-006 cipher already imports node:crypto, so adding timingSafeEqual here doesn't add weight. (6) Returned 503 when env.CRON_SECRET is unset rather than 401 — this is misconfiguration, not unauthorized; UptimeRobot/cron operators can distinguish 'I forgot to set the env' from 'someone is hitting this without a token'. Verification (per architectural_principles 'Тесты пишем ТОЛЬКО для streak calculation и token crypto. CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file added): wrote temporary app/api/cron/check-deadlines/_smoke.test.ts (5 vitest cases, deleted after run) covering all four PRD test_steps + edge cases. Created a test User and 5 challenges (active+past+unmet, active+past+met, active+future+unmet, completed+past, archived+past). Ran with shell-overridden env vars (DATABASE_URL/NEXTAUTH_*/GOOGLE_*/CRON_SECRET) since .env.local has the known TASK-003 NEXTAUTH_URL typo. Results: (1) no Bearer → 401; (2) wrong-token Bearer → 401; (3) same-length-different-bytes Bearer → 401 (timingSafeEqual works); (4) valid Bearer → 200, response.processed >= 1, only the active+past+unmet row flipped to 'failed' — past+met stayed active (target met, must be recalc'd to 'completed' by TASK-019, not failed by deadline), future+unmet stayed active (deadline not reached), already-completed stayed completed, already-archived stayed archived; (5) idempotent — second call → processed: 0. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run build (with shell-overridden env: route registered as ƒ /api/cron/check-deadlines, server-rendered on demand).

Грейс-период: если сегодня ещё нет активности, current = streak до вчера; если вчера тоже нет — current=0
longest: максимальная длина серии за всю историю
Чистая функция, принимает массив activities
Использует date-fns-tz для корректных timezone границ (день начинается/заканчивается в timezone пользователя)
Unit-тесты: пустой массив → 0/0; одна активность сегодня → 1/1; 3 дня подряд → 3/3; пропуск посередине → текущий стрик меньше longest; смена месяца/года; смена timezone
test_steps: Все unit-тесты проходят
Активности в дни 26.04, 27.04, 28.04, 29.04 (сегодня 29.04 MSK) → current=4
Активности 26.04, 27.04, 29.04 (пропуск 28.04) → current=1, longest=2
tasks.notes: lib/services/streaks.ts exports calculateStreak(activities, userTz='Europe/Moscow', now=new Date()) -> {current, longest}. Pure function, no I/O. Activities are bucketed by UTC calendar day because Activity.activityDate is @db.Date (UTC-midnight per Prisma's Date deserialization — verified in schema.prisma line 133). 'Today' is computed in the user's tz via date-fns-tz formatInTimeZone(now, tz, 'yyyy-MM-dd'); the asymmetry between UTC bucketing and user-tz today is intentional and correct since @db.Date stores a calendar day with no time component, so today-in-user-tz vs activity-day-in-UTC is calendar-day-vs-calendar-day. Grace period implemented: if today has no activity, fall back to yesterday-in-user-tz; if yesterday is also empty, current=0. Longest is computed by sorting day keys (yyyy-MM-dd lex order matches chronological) and tracking the longest run of consecutive days. Day arithmetic uses Date.UTC + setUTCDate to avoid DST ambiguity. 16 unit tests in lib/services/streaks.test.ts cover: empty array (0/0), single activity today (1/1), 3 consecutive (3/3), PRD examples (4/4 and 1/2-with-gap), grace period (today empty, yesterday active), neither today nor yesterday active (current=0, longest preserved), duplicate same-day activities deduped, month transition (Jan->Feb), year transition (Dec->Jan), late-evening UTC that's next-day in MSK, early-morning UTC that's previous-day in LA, multiple separate runs (longest=5 not current=1), input ordering invariance, default-tz behavior, input-array purity (no mutation). Verification (all clean): npm test 26/26 passing (10 cipher + 16 streaks), npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run format:check. Note on toolchain: user prompt asks for `uv run ruff check` / `uv run pytest` but this is a TS/Next.js project — used npm equivalents (ESLint / tsc / vitest). Pre-existing files in working tree from a prior partial iteration; this iteration verified correctness, applied prettier formatting, and confirmed all acceptance criteria.

tasks.notes: lib/services/dashboard.ts exports getDashboardData(userId, options?) -> DashboardData. Pure aggregation: composes calculateStreak (TASK-021), prisma.challenge.findMany twice (active + completed-take-5), getTodayWater (TASK-027), getLatestWeight (TASK-029), and an in-memory heatmap derived from the same activities array as the streak. All five DB calls run in a single Promise.all — verified one round-trip per service via the smoke. options: { userTz?: string, heatmapDays?: number, now?: Date } — sensible defaults (DEFAULT_USER_TZ='Europe/Moscow' from streaks.ts, heatmapDays=365 per PRD desktop default, now=new Date() for testability). Caller (e.g. dashboard page in TASK-023+) can pass heatmapDays=90 for mobile. Design choices worth flagging: (1) Activities are fetched ONCE for both streak and heatmap, with `select: { activityDate: true }` to keep the row narrow. The streak calc needs full history (longest is 'максимальная за всю историю' per PRD), and the heatmap filters in memory to the trailing N days — single query is correct given PRD's single-user-low-volume scale. If a future user crosses ~10k activities, splitting into two queries (full date range for streak metadata + narrow window for heatmap counts) is a pure perf swap and won't change the public shape. (2) Heatmap buckets by UTC day key (formatUtcDayKey), matching the streak calc's existing UTC bucketing of @db.Date activityDates — this asymmetry-with-user-tz-today is documented in TASK-021 progress and is correct because Activity.activityDate is stored as UTC midnight calendar day. (3) Heatmap returns ONLY days with activity (no zero-fill) — same convention as listWaterByDay. UI consumer (TASK-026 ActivityHeatmap) zero-fills cells. (4) Active challenges ordered by [endDate asc, createdAt desc] — most-urgent-first surfaces deadlines, ties broken by recency. recentAchievements ordered by [completedAt desc, createdAt desc] with take:5. The completedAt-first sort handles the case where two challenges complete in different sessions; createdAt is the tiebreaker for older completions where completedAt is identical (e.g., backfill). (5) waterToday and weightLatest delegated to existing services to avoid duplicating the tz/upsert/delta logic. Cost is two extra DB round-trips inside Promise.all (waterLog.aggregate + userSettings.findUnique within getTodayWater; weightLog.findMany within getLatestWeight) — fine on small data, and keeps a single source of truth for those formulas. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. SHARED HELPERS EXTRACTION (third-callsite threshold met, per TASK-027 progress notes): created lib/utils/date-tz.ts with formatUserTzDayKey / formatUtcDayKey / shiftDayKey / userTzDayBounds. Refactored lib/services/streaks.ts and lib/services/water.ts to import from there (removed inlined helpers). Streak tests still pass 16/16 — pure-function refactor only. The pure module has NO server-only or prisma imports so it's importable from both server services and pure unit tests (matches challenge-progress.ts split pattern). tasks.description: Service для WaterLog: lib/services/water.ts + zod схема
acceptance_criteria: Zod schema: addWaterSchema { amountMl: int > 0 }
Service: addWater(userId, amountMl), getTodayWater(userId, tz) → { consumed, goal }, listWaterByDay(userId, days) → [{date, total}], deleteWater(userId, id)
getTodayWater сравнивает с user_settings.water_daily_goal_ml

getTodayWater после двух addWater по 250 — consumed=500
Записи вчерашнего дня не учитываются в today
deleteWater — запись удалена
tasks.notes: lib/validation/water.ts exports addWaterSchema = z.object({ amountMl: int positive }) and the inferred AddWaterInput type. lib/services/water.ts exports addWater / getTodayWater / listWaterByDay / deleteWater plus TodayWater and WaterByDay interfaces. All functions take userId first and scope every where-clause for IDOR (same pattern as challenges.ts/activities.ts). Design choices: (1) WaterLog.loggedAt is `DateTime @default(now())` — full timestamp, NOT @db.Date. So 'today' is computed as a tz-aware UTC interval rather than a calendar-day equality. getTodayWater(userId, tz='Europe/Moscow', now=new Date()) computes user-tz day bounds via fromZonedTime(`${todayKey}T00:00:00.000`, tz) for both ends — this handles DST correctly (a wall-clock day in user-tz can be 23/24/25 hours; fromZonedTime resolves the wall-clock-to-UTC instant per the IANA tz database). The 'tomorrow' boundary uses the next user-tz calendar day, NOT start+24h. (2) listWaterByDay(userId, days, tz='Europe/Moscow', now) groups by user-tz YYYY-MM-DD key. Returns ONLY days with logs (no zero-fill) — UI consumer (TASK-028 chart) is responsible for zero-filling if it wants a continuous bar chart. Empty days don't waste DB rows or wire bandwidth. days<=0 short-circuits to []. (3) tz/now are optional with sensible defaults so callers without a session-user-tz still work — DEFAULT_USER_TZ='Europe/Moscow' is imported from streaks.ts (single source of truth, matches PRD's single-user assumption). 'now' is injectable for testability. (4) getTodayWater uses prisma.waterLog.aggregate({_sum: {amountMl}}) for a server-side SUM — single round-trip, no in-memory aggregation. _sum returns null when no rows match; coalesced to 0. (5) UserSettings goal lookup runs in parallel with the aggregate via Promise.all. Falls back to DEFAULT_WATER_GOAL_ML=2000 if no settings row (defensive — UserSettings should always exist post-TASK-007 signIn callback, but better to return a sane default than crash). 2000 matches schema.prisma:88 default. (6) deleteWater follows challenges.ts's findFirst-then-delete pattern: returns null cleanly on cross-user/nonexistent. (7) addWater is a plain create — no recalculateChallengeProgress call (water doesn't feed Challenge.metric mappings; only Activity does). (8) Helpers shiftDayKey + userTzDayBounds are inlined rather than extracted to a shared lib/utils/date module — same 5-line shape exists in streaks.ts and the architectural_principles say 'no premature abstraction'. Two callsites is below the threshold; if a third lands (e.g., TASK-029 weight or TASK-022 dashboard), pull both into lib/utils/date-tz.ts then. (9) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. Per architectural_principles 'Тесты пишем ТОЛЬКО для streak calculation и token crypto. CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. Verified via temporary lib/services/_smoke-water.test.ts (6 vitest cases against live Neon, deleted after run): addWater persists row with amountMl/userId; getTodayWater sums today's logs (250+250=500) and reads UserSettings.waterDailyGoalMl=2500; yesterday's row (loggedAt set to UTC noon yesterday) is NOT in today's sum (500 stays 500); listWaterByDay(7) returns 2 buckets (today=500, yesterday=9999) — total across days matches; getTodayWater on a user without UserSettings returns goal=2000 (DEFAULT fallback) and consumed=0; deleteWater cross-user returns null without removing, owner removes row. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress), npm run build (with shell-overridden env since .env.local has the known TASK-003 NEXTAUTH_URL typo + a quoted-string parse issue at line 31).

tasks.description: Service для WeightLog: lib/services/weight.ts + zod схема
acceptance_criteria: Zod schema: logWeightSchema { weightKg: float > 0 < 500, measuredAt: date, note? }
Service: logWeight(userId, input) — upsert по (userId, measuredAt) (одна запись на день), getLatestWeight(userId) → { value, delta, measuredAt }, listWeights(userId, days), deleteWeight(userId, id)
delta = последний - предпоследний
test_steps: logWeight 75.5 на сегодня — запись создана
logWeight 76.0 на сегодня — запись обновлена (не вторая запись)
logWeight на вчера 74.0 → getLatestWeight возвращает delta=+1.5 (75.5 - 74.0)
deleteWeight удаляет
tasks.notes: lib/validation/weight.ts exports logWeightSchema { weightKg: float positive() lt(500), measuredAt: z.coerce.date(), note: trim().max(500).optional() } and inferred LogWeightInput. lib/services/weight.ts exports logWeight / getLatestWeight / listWeights / deleteWeight plus LatestWeight interface. All functions take userId first and scope every where-clause for IDOR (same pattern as challenges.ts/activities.ts/water.ts). Design choices: (1) WeightLog.measuredAt is @db.Date with @@unique([userId, measuredAt]) (verified schema.prisma:161,167), so 'one weight per day' is enforced at the DB layer. logWeight uses prisma.weightLog.upsert by the compound unique key (Prisma 7 generates `userId_measuredAt`) — single round-trip, no findFirst-then-update dance, race-safe. Same convention as Activity.activityDate and Challenge.startDate/endDate: UTC-midnight = calendar day, tz normalization is the caller's responsibility (see TASK-016/017/021 progress notes). (2) toUtcMidnight helper extracts UTC year/month/day so a Date with non-zero time-of-day collapses to that day's UTC midnight. With z.coerce.date() turning 'YYYY-MM-DD' into UTC midnight already, this is idempotent for the canonical form. (3) getLatestWeight does a single findMany with take:2 / orderBy measuredAt desc, then returns { value: latest.weightKg, delta: latest - previous (or null if only one row), measuredAt: latest.measuredAt }. delta=null when there's no previous row was the choice flagged in TASK-027's 'next iteration' notes ('null is more honest than 0' — PRD doesn't specify). Returns null entirely if no rows. (4) listWeights(userId, days, now=new Date()) computes start = Date.UTC(now.year, now.month, now.day - days + 1) so days=7 includes [today-6, today]. days<=0 short-circuits to []. orderBy measuredAt desc matches getLatestWeight's contract (newest first; UI can reverse for chart). (5) deleteWeight uses the challenges.ts findFirst-then-delete pattern: returns null cleanly on cross-user / nonexistent. (6) `import 'server-only'` at top blocks accidental client bundle inclusion. (7) Note field accepts `note ?? null` in upsert update/create payload — z.coerce.date() infers `note: string | undefined`, but Prisma WeightLog.note is `String?` (nullable). Coercing undefined to null at the service boundary keeps Prisma's input narrow and explicit; an undefined update would leave the existing note unchanged (different semantics). Since logWeight is upsert-by-day, treating absent note as 'clear it' is the natural read of the input. (8) Helpers (toUtcMidnight) inlined per architectural_principles 'no premature abstraction' — same shape as in streaks.ts/water.ts, but tz-aware bucketing isn't needed here because measuredAt is already a calendar-day field. When TASK-022 wires the dashboard agg with tz-aware day buckets across streaks/water/weight/heatmap, that's the right time to extract a shared lib/utils/date-tz.ts (already flagged in TASK-027's next-iteration notes). Per architectural_principles 'CRUD не покрываем unit-тестами' — no permanent test file. Verified all 4 PRD test_steps via temporary lib/services/_smoke-weight.test.ts (6 vitest cases against live Neon, deleted after run): test_step 1+2: logWeight 75.5 today → row created (id assigned, weightKg=75.5); logWeight 76.0 same day → SAME id, weightKg=76.0, only 1 row in DB (compound unique upsert update branch). test_step 3: logWeight 75.5 today + 74.0 yesterday → getLatestWeight returns value=75.5, delta=1.5, measuredAt=today. Edge: getLatestWeight with only 1 row → delta=null (not 0, not undefined). Edge: getLatestWeight with 0 rows → null. listWeights: 3 rows (today/yesterday/8-days-ago) with days=7 returns only the 2 within window, ordered desc. test_step 4: deleteWeight cross-user returns null and the row remains in DB; owner deleteWeight returns the row and findUnique afterwards confirms removal. Build gates clean: npm run typecheck, npm run lint, npm run format:check, npm test (44/44 unaffected: 10 cipher + 16 streaks + 18 progress).
